brief: Two bins to sort my dead AA batteries for recycling.

requirements.requirement: Two bins to sort dead AA batteries
requirements.evidence: Two separate full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full, on adjoining bases piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full, bolted together (jointBolt) and end-capped. Each bin floor is 142x124mm, ample for AA cells lying down.

Shape is an open collection bin pair for sorting (e.g. ready-to-recycle vs. awaiting tape/test); configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about materials, leakage or battery-storage safety, so terminal-taping, leak/corrosion resistance and any local recycling rules are for the user — tape dead AA terminals and do not mix damaged/leaking cells.

finish.summary: Built a two-cell Hex Cluster unit: two adjoining full bases, each holding a plain full-depth bin (142x124mm floor, ~77mm deep) so dead AA batteries can be sorted into two separate piles for recycling. Open faces capped with solid end caps and the joint bolted. No AA-battery prop exists in the catalog and the closest heap props would hide below the rim and misrepresent the contents, so the bins are left empty and ready to fill. Note: tape the terminals of dead AAs and keep damaged/leaking cells out — material/chemical safety is outside what the configurator can verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Two bins for dead AAs — I'll check the current build and find battery-sized bins and props to stage them.
